comments.text:
The Jaguar CPU in 16nm is extremely power efficient @1.6 ghz, like in the ps4 pro slim. They used slower transistors that use less power, also went for 8 simpler cores that use 1/2 as many transistors as a quad core with the same performance @ the same clock, resulting in about 1/8th the power consumption of an equivalent performance 3.2ghz i3. The problem with transistor speed, is that they have an optimum operational range. You can have transistors designed to have the lowest possible power consumption @100mhz, and they will use less power than transistors designed to run @1ghz and then downclocked. However, if you want to make the slower transistor reach something like 500mhz, you will need so much voltage that the 1ghz processor may end up using less power and being more powerful (that's why some mobile gpu's can have a thousand little cores running @300mhz).
 Back to the jaguar in the PRO, increasing the clocks to 2.5ghz would not make the CPU use 50% more power than the base ps4 slim, but 2.4 to 2.5 times as much. This would reduce the performance per watt, but we should consider 2 points regarding this: they can''t switch architecture, but they must have used slightly different transistors for the pro vs the slim, and the power delivery + cooling system was designed for the newer 2.1ghz chip. if that is the case, increasing the clock to 2.5 ghz would result in little over 40% more power consumption. You may think that's a lot, but we are talking about a processor that only uses a couple of watts and is sharing a die with a rather massive gpu. 
 Regarding the GPU, it's an RX 480. Desktop parts overclock up to 1.4ghz and most non refference cooler versions boost to 1.3ghz by themselves. Reference design boosts to 1.266mhz. Non-reference boards have a base clock of 1.2+ ghz and reference boards do 1120mhz. The 1086mhz necessary to reach 5tflops are well within the ps4 pro's power envelope.
